content.user_title: Plan Tasks with Practical Quality Gates
content.value_statement: Unclear requirements and repeated failed attempts can waste time and create unreliable work. This skill provides repeatable checks for complexity, dependencies, evidence, and escalation before work continues.
actual_capabilities: Scores task complexity on a five-level scale using scope, dependencies, and unknowns.
Identifies unanswered critical questions before implementation begins.
Provides gate templates for dependencies, failed attempts, and completion evidence.
Recommends escalation after repeated failed attempts or unresolved blockers.
Breaks complex work into smaller subtasks with dependencies and acceptance criteria.
Checks functional and technical requirements for completeness.
limitations: It provides planning guidance and does not execute tests, builds, or deployments.
Complexity scores and estimates require informed human or agent judgment.
It cannot confirm that external dependencies are available without supplied evidence.
The three-attempt escalation threshold may need adjustment for a specific team.

use_cases.title: Clarify a feature before coding
use_cases.description: Use a gate check to identify missing behavior, dependencies, and acceptance criteria before starting implementation.

use_cases.title: Break down a large delivery
use_cases.description: Turn a complex project into smaller tasks with mapped dependencies and evidence checkpoints.

use_cases.title: Escalate a blocked agent task
use_cases.description: Document failed approaches and ask focused questions after repeated attempts do not resolve a problem.

prompt_templates.title: Run a basic gate check
prompt_templates.prompt: Run a quality gate for this task: [task]. Assess complexity, list critical questions, identify dependencies, and state whether work can proceed.

prompt_templates.title: Review requirements
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the requirements completeness checklist for [feature]. Identify missing happy-path, error-handling, input-validation, API, and security requirements.

prompt_templates.title: Break down complex work
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess [project] as a Level 4 or 5 task. Create Level 1 to 3 subtasks with dependencies, acceptance criteria, estimates, and gate checks.

prompt_templates.title: Escalate a repeated failure
prompt_templates.prompt: I tried [task] three times. Summarize each approach and outcome, identify the current blocker, and draft focused questions for human guidance.

output_examples.input: Assess a new payment settings page before implementation.
output: Complexity: Level 4 because authentication, payment integration, and several components are involved.
Gate status: Blocked until payment provider requirements and error scenarios are confirmed.
Next action: Create subtasks and clarify the API contract.

output_examples.input: Review a task that failed three implementation attempts.
output: Gate status: Blocked after three failed attempts.
Escalation summary: List each approach, its failure reason, and the persistent blocker.
Next action: Ask the owner to confirm the expected behavior and available dependencies.

best_practices: Run a short gate check before every task and a full check before complex work.
Record assumptions, dependencies, and evidence with the task decision.
Escalate with specific questions after repeated failures instead of repeating the same approach.
anti_patterns: Starting a complex task without a breakdown or acceptance criteria.
Treating warning status as approval without documenting assumptions.
Continuing after a blocked gate without resolving the stated blocker.

faq.question: What is a quality gate?
faq.answer: A quality gate is a short decision process that checks whether a task has enough information and evidence to proceed.

faq.question: When should I use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it before new work, when requirements are unclear, when dependencies are missing, or after repeated failed attempts.

faq.question: How does the complexity scale work?
faq.answer: The skill uses levels 1 through 5 based on scope, dependencies, unknowns, and estimated effort.

faq.question: What blocks a task?
faq.answer: More than three critical unknowns, missing dependencies, repeated failures, failed evidence, or an unplanned complex task block progress.

faq.question: Does this skill run tests or builds?
faq.answer: No. It helps define and evaluate required evidence, but another tool must run tests and builds.

faq.question: Can I change the gate thresholds?
faq.answer: Yes. Adapt the thresholds, complexity criteria, and escalation path to your team and project context.
